questions.q: What does the "Interface" in API refer to?
options: The visual design of a website
The specific, documented set of requests an application has agreed to understand and respond to
A type of database
The programming language used to build the application
questions.explain: The Interface is the documented point of contact — the specific requests the application will accept and answer.

questions.q: In this course, which software is "the Application" that the API gives access to?
options: A generic reporting tool
Oracle Fusion Cloud Financials
A spreadsheet program
The student's own laptop
questions.explain: This course is about Oracle Fusion Financials' REST APIs specifically.

questions.q: A program retrieves an invoice's amount via a REST API call instead of a user looking it up on screen. What is true about the underlying data?
options: It is a completely different copy of the invoice stored separately for APIs
It does not exist until the API is called
It is the same underlying data, reached through a different door
APIs can only return fake sample data, never real records
questions.explain: The API and the UI are two different doors into the same underlying application data.

questions.q: Which of these is a realistic reason a Financials consultant would care about Oracle Fusion's REST APIs?
options: To change the color scheme of the Oracle Fusion login page
To let an external system create or update invoices and journals without manual re-entry
To bypass all security and validation rules
To avoid ever logging into Oracle Fusion again
questions.explain: A core real-world use is inbound data loads and outbound extracts that remove manual re-entry.

questions.q: True or false: An API is a separate software product you install, unrelated to the application it exposes.
options: True — APIs are standalone products
False — an API is a documented way to access an existing application's data and functions, not a separate product
True, but only for cloud applications
False, because APIs only work with databases, never applications
questions.explain: An API is a contract/interface into an existing application, not a separate installable product.
